TextEng: This jagged piece of rock is ill-balanced for a sling bullet but it will still serve to take down your prey from afar.
You stare at the ragged seagull's feather, deep in thought. You wonder what you could fashion out of it.
The tip of this crude wooden spear has been hardened to a charred point.
This glob of smelly ichor sticks to your fingers as you handle it. You wonder if it has any particular use.
Fashioned from uncured hide, this ragged sling is nevertheless a useful means of striking at your opponents from afar.
This weathered piece of driftwood should make an adequate club. It's dry enough to serve as firewood, as well. You wonder if there's anything else you could use it for.
This talking bird claims that her name is Jaeda, a druid who was cursed and polymorphed into a chicken.

A concoction of essential oils, musks and base notes mixed to a specification invented by the Rashemi trader known as 'White Glove', this perfume creates such a stir that its wearer will likely find their words most well received by listeners.
This is the rod of detection given to you by Astriel in order to detect anything that is normally un-detectable at the Black Stone Inn.

Strange wisps of pale grey smoke, like the thick fog that hugs a graveyard at night, swirl menacingly inside this large glass orb. The orb is affixed to its heavy silver base by five slender claws; the tip of each claw is carved to resemble a cloven hoof.

Once a Devil, such as a Baatezu, has been weakened by the loss of at least half of its maximum hit points, it can be trapped inside an Orb of Devil Containment. Once trapped, the unfortunate Devil cannot free itself until the Orb is broken. Each Orb of Devil Containment can trap only a single Devil.

This magnificent helm belonged to the ancient dwarven royalty of Illefarn. It was lost for many ages following the collapse of the Fallen Kingdom. Despite untold ages spent in obscurity, it still gleams with flawless dwarven craftsmanship.

The note reads:

You are one of the elite few, Chosen of Gorgomorz, to strike the first blow against the piddling human town of Daggerford! Lead your troops through the tunnel and into the castle cellars but do not slay those in the castle...yet. Control your battle-lust and stay hidden there until the next night. Disobey and the Master shall roast you alive when he finds you! When night falls, sneak out from the castle, kill the guards at the west gate and open the gates for our army. Glory to the fires that shall burn! Glory to the blood we shall shed! Glory to almighty Gorgomorz!

Long ago, near the ancient shores of Torslunda, an old poet dwelled alone in crumbling Daargard Keep. Each night, by flickering candlelight, the old poet labored to wrap his thoughts in ink and verse. Already blind with age, the poet felt the bitter kiss of fate, for he lived long enough to touch his beloved son's grave stone. In the dark keep, upon rows of faded scrolls, the old poet patiently scribed his stories using powerful runes of blood.

Many long years later, a noble Lord and Lady departed on an epic island adventure, and arrived upon the shores of ancient Torslunda. The Lord and Lady explored the forgotten ruins of Daargard Keep, and discovered several of the blind poet's scrolls. These treasured works of art have been passed carefully from generation to generation so that the old poet's colorful songs have entertained and inspired hundreds of hopeful adventurers across many lands.

Each of the blind poet's songs is about a different theme. This particular song is about the old poet's fear of death. When sung by a bard, the bard gains a brief mastery over death, and his nearby enemies suffer damage.
This talking parrot insists that it is really a druid named Wanix. The parrot has asked you to take it to Govan's Stone Circle in the Brush of Barbs.
This talking penguin claims to be an elven druid named Urith. She has asked you to return her to Govan's Stone Circle in the Brush of Barbs.
The corpse of Fernigold the Younger.
This chest contains something or someone, that has asked you to return it to Delfen at the Sorceller's Encapsulate.
Given to you by Delfen, this chest contains a special something that will be a 'nice' surprise for Mogdor when it is delivered to him.

The note reads:

The plans are going as intended.
The operations room has been set up in the sewer under the Black Stone Inn.

The key will allow you access to the operations room.

The Archmage Leomund created this magic rod so that he would always have a secure place to rest after battle. The rod opens a portal to a private pocket dimension where you can rest and recover from battle.

This thick ledger contains shipping records which detail the Shoreside Shipping Consortium's business along the River Delimbiyr. One of their ships, the Barracuda, has been transporting many shipments of weapons and armor, however, the ship's final destination is never mentioned. The Barracuda, under the stalwart command of Captain Herab, is currently docked here in Daggerford.

The note is sealed with a thin strip of red wax. Cracking open the wax seal reveals the evil plans of a nefarious organization called the Zhentarim. 

The Zhentarim, also known as the Black Network, is an evil organization seeking to dominate the lands from the Moonsea to the Sword Coast.

Working in secret, these Zhentarim have prepared weapons and armor for a rampaging army of orcs, and have even struck a deal with a devil.

At the bottom of the note there is also mention of a secret Zhentarim base somewhere in the region.
This is the key to the Gillian's Hill graveyard crypt given to you by Farmer Callaway.

This note reads:

As per our agreement, simply escort the halfling and his cart to Gillian's Hill. If there's any trouble, improvise.

The note is signed with a large red "Y."

Lord Alex, famed highway bandit and pub-crawling pontificator, had his wizardly friend Cathexis devise for him a magic ale-mug that never runs dry. Each time the vessel is drained of its contents, the stein instantly refills itself to the brim with a bounteous helping of dark, frothy stout.
One of the new Mariners uniforms given to you by Falias

This smooth, golden chalice is completely without adornment except for the strange maze-like pattern etched into its base. To someone who studies such things, this pattern would instantly identify the item as being from the fabled city of Mezro that lies deep within the jungles of Chult. This chalice, and others like it, are used by the fabled Mazewalkers of Mezro who are clerics in the service of the Chultan deity, Ubtao. Legends claim that if someone not in the service of Ubtao stares overlong at the maze design etched into the chalice they will eventually go mad.
This sack of gold is meant for Millie Churlgo and is payment for cheese delivered to Sejellus Krimp.
This is a receipt for a bill of goods sold to Sejellus Krimp and payment made to Millie Churlgo for 500 gold pieces.

Gravia's Hot Apple Cider

Ingredients:

1/2 gallon apple juice
2 cinnamon sticks
2 whole cloves
2 allspice berries
1/2 orange peel, cut into strips
1/2 lemon peel, cut into strips
Special ingredient (see note below)

Directions:

1. Pour apple juice into a large pot.
2. Wrap spices and peels in a thin, porous cloth.
3. Drop cloth into apple juice.
4. Heat juice to a boil and then slow cook for two hours.
5. Remove cloth.
6. Add the special ingredient.
7. Serve hot!

Note: A fellow named Stran in the Black Stone Inn sells "knockout drops," which are added to the cider immediately before presenting it to "the victim."

This robe gives off a strong scent of formaldehyde, as if it's been worn by someone skilled in embalming and treatment of the dead.

The robe's former owner, a necromancer named Daxiong, pioneered new advances in the art of zombification. Daxiong imbued the garment with magic to ward off the undead, just in case one of his "test subjects" turned on its master.
This is an almost exact replica of a famous painting of Duke Greatshout.
Fake Portrait: "Greatshout as a Young Man"

Servants of the Morninglord often bestow these amulets on devotees who have peformed a special service or duty for the Church of Lathander. In addition to its inherent value (the amulets are often made of solid gold), these trinkets tend to also provide some modest magical benefit, as well.
This is a light white wine from Mistledale.

Tasting like it was scraped off the bottom of the Sea of Swords, this rot-gut whiskey is also one of the more potent spirits one can buy. This makes it a favorite among sailors seeking to get drunk cheaply and quickly.
This is a minty ale from Highcastle.
Just holding this bottle gives one a sense of peace and well-being. It must have been a powerful deity indeed to have infused this vial of holy water with a piece of its divinity.

This weighty magnifying glass has a half-inch thick lens. It allows its user to zoom in on common objects to find runes or codes that identify an item's hidden origins.

As with the Identify spell, the player character should be the target when using the item, not the object being identified.
This key opens the basement in the Bricket house.

Across the top of this perfumed journal, written in a flowery prose, is the name "Alicine Bricket."

Most of the entries describe her ongoing feud with her brother Elveronne over management of the family estate and the repayment of various long-standing debts.

However, one recent entry catches your eye that specifically mentions Elveronne's death and recent funeral:

"I've got it! Elveronne's necklace is mine, the thing I've longed for since it first came into his possession. I don't believe anyone saw me either. I merely bent down over his coffin to give him a farewell kiss and slipped it in a fold in my dress! I really can be a proficient pickpocket when the need is great.

Oh, the bliss I now feel is indescribable. To think I've managed to take from him in death the one thing he valued so much in life. It's one tiny morsel of revenge that I can nibble on daily until I too am committed to that musty old tomb. You deserve far worse than this, Elveronne Bricket, but this will have to do for now."

Written at the top of this leather-bound tome, in a rough, barely-legible hand, are the words: "Elveronne's Journal"

From the contents, you surmise this to be the last of a series of journals kept by the late Elveronne Bricket. Of the entries you can make out, most detail his increasing conflicts with his two sisters, Muriel and Alicine, whom he describes as "money-grubbing loafers" and "unworthy of bearing the name 'Bricket.'" Some entries even hint at "plotting" by Muriel and Alicine to undercut his authority.

However, not all the entries deal with his scheming sisters. One entry, in particular, shows a more poignant side to Elveronne Bricket, as he mourns the failed outcome of a youthful relationship:

"When shall it end, this pain I feel? I am cursed, it seems, to think upon her loveliness for the rest of my days... and beyond. I can still see her face, ringed with sunlight, as her jade-colored eyes met mine for the very first time. Ours would have been a joyful union had her father not forbade us from seeing one another.

The last day I beheld her face... oh, the pain of it still stings me to the core... She was so lovely... a pure, elven maid of the wood. Tears filled her eyes, as she gave me the necklace. I vowed to keep it close, and it is a vow I shall take with me to the grave...."

This lovely necklace gives off a strange, otherworldly glow, as if it contains some spiritual essence within its metal. A small locket is attached that when opened reveals the painted image of a beautiful elven maid.
From the pungent odor and skull and crossbones emblem across the front, you easily identify the liquid in this vial as poison.
This delectable cake is sweet and bread-like with crushed anise, caraway, and coriander seeds.
This sturdy, silver-plated awl is perfectly balanced with a long sharpened point. A skilled woodworker could use such a tool to great effect.

This bitter-tasting elixir, invented by Zakharan physicians as a potent cure for insomnia, is made by combining animal fats, prunes, oranges, sugar, and salt into a clear syrup that dissolves in water, alcohol, and olive oil. When ingested, the drug's active ingredients result in a near-instantaneous (and very deep) sleep. This armor consists of polished bark covered with a fine weave of silk from spiders that nest within Chult's highest trees. The arachnid properties of the armor grant the user complete immunity to poison and web-based spell effects.

This book is filled with strange, incoherent markings that seem to be representative of some foreign language. However, a few of the more recent passages are written in the common tongue:

Strange that I've begun to think and write in the language of humanoids, since I've only been on Toril for a scant few months. Their language, as with every other aspect of their culture, is so very, very primitive. These humanoids are children...sheep...and ripe for the slaughter!

Once this miller begins to mix my toxins into his flour and spread it amongst the locals in the area, I'll have a small army of slaadi to do my bidding...

In fact, so wretched is her singing voice, that her long-time lover and adventuring companion, Lord Alex, had a special lute designed as a gag gift for her birthday. The sound it makes renders creatures helpless with pain and frequently causes bleeding from the ears, much like Lady Oonagh's singing.
These humanoid bones are scarred and damaged, as if they've been gnawed upon by some malevolent entity.

A lesser variant of the knight's blade or Holy Avenger, this sword was blessed by a high priest of Torm. If the wielder be pure of heart, the sword is an effective weapon against the denizens of evil.

This is an odd bluish-gray statue of a large bear rearing up on its hind legs. Those with knowledge of the Uthgardt barbarians, would instantly recognize this as an Uthgardt burial totem taken from the Stone Stand, the infamous ancestral mound of the long-dead Blue Bear tribe. This worn and weather-beaten tome has had all but the very last entry torn out, as if the author intentionally destroyed all record of their prior thoughts or achievements. The final entry is written in a hurried, erratic fashion, which might call into question the author's sanity:

Fifteen years ago, when I finalized my doctrine on Theorosophy, I never dreamed it would morph into the abomination that now plagues me so. The initial concept was sound: that one should not discount deep, psychic urges and the motivations of the unconscious mind when attempting to validate an unproven hypothesis. Too often, science ignores a creature's base, primeval desires, and instead chooses to place too much importance on facts and clinical data.

Where I went wrong was in my attempts to translate this new approach to my pupils, a couple of fawning, inept university rejects named Beb-Shuur and Xianga. These two brainless nitwits seem less concerned with the "meaning" of my words than with the syntax. For example, although I desired to apply more weight to emotions and ideals, they've chosen to do so by forsaking the primary intent of philosophical theory, which is to prove a hypothesis using factual data.

Instead, the blathering idiots use empiricism simply to bolster their twisted, quasi-spiritual view of the world and have begun promoting this new pseudo-science in all the trade journals. Worse still, they've named me as their mentor, which has drastically reduced my standing within the philosophical community.

My reputation is in tatters and without that, I am nothing...

The Treatise of Suffering
Author: Unknown

Life is pain. The suffering begins at childbirth and ends when we gasp our final breath. As disciples in Bhaal's order, it is our duty to remind the heathens that pain is the essence of life and provides the only true path to salvation.

Cries of agony ring like musical notes in the ears of our Dread Lord. The cries of children, in particular, provide our Master with great joy for they represent anguish in its purest form, freed from the bonds of duty and convention. Each time a child cries out in pain, our Master feels a sensation akin to rapture.

As shepherds in the service of Bhaal, it is our sworn duty to see that the cries of the living reach our Master's ears. At times, this may involve intensifying or prolonging the suffering of our "flock." Bhaal has decreed that the reward for our dutiful service shall be nothing less than a life free of pain, except for that issued at Bhaal's command.

For those disciples who have mistakenly allied themselves against Bhaal's plan for salvation, there is no recourse but pain, administered at its highest threshold. We must let their cries ring out loud and long, so our Master may channel misery into bliss.

Life is pain. All praise the Lord of Murder!

This appears to be the journal of the temple of Bhaal's high priest. Most of the book details the gruesome ritual activities of the clergy over a number of years leading up to the Time of Troubles. Only the last few entries seem to be of interest:

13 Ches, 1358
A public sacrifice to Bhaal has increased the religious fervor of the faithful. The woman was burned in the town square under the guise of a witch. Her screams of torment may even find her a place in the afterlife.

25 Ches, 1358
I was required to trim our order as a traitor was amongst us, so says the messenger of Bhaal. Our blood pools are restocked and at least four faithful have moved on to their rewards. Regardless of whether we have actually trimmed the traitor from our midst, the display was poignant.

4 Tarsakh, 1358
It has been a night blessed by Bhaal. We returned with five children, all of which shall please Bhaal in various fashions. The morning light broke with screams reaching our ears. Yes, blessed be Bhaal!

16 Eleint, 1358
The mass was interrupted this eve by an invading force of humans, elves, and animals, who all exuded the disgusting stench of nature. These infidels caused considerable damage to the inner temple walls, and killed several priests before we repelled them. Bhaal shall require much satiating for this affront. We will take revenge upon these intruders, but first, I must find an appropriate sacrifice.

17 Eleint, 1358
As if the previous night's sacrilege against Bhaal was not enough, this morning has brought more misfortune. Something truly perplexing has occurred. It is as if Bhaal's gaze upon us has simply vanished, as he no longer answers our prayers. I am at a loss to explain this and the ritual sacrifice done thrice over appears not to have helped matters. We have sent word to the temple in Waterdeep in search of an explanation. In the meantime, I have safely secured all of the temple's most precious treasures in the secret vault. Hopefully an answer to this mystery is forthcoming...

This is the journal's final entry, followed by blank pages until the end of the book.

Cheesy Skewers

Ingredients:

5 rats
5 skewers
1 bucket
1 basket
Goat cheese
Salt 
Beer
Oil

Directions:

1. Drink pint of beer. 
2. Put cheese on ground and hide nearby.
3. Drink another beer while hiding.
4. When rat goes for cheese, capture with bucket and put in basket. 
5. Repeat until all rats are captured. 
6. Drop cheese in basket with rats so they eat it all up and get fat.
7. Drink another beer.
8. Skewer rats, dip in beer (if any left), and roll in salt.
9. Put skewered rats in hot oil until fur all singed off.
10. Serve with beer for dipping.

History of Daggerford

Daggerford was founded along the Trade Way, at the major crossing of the River Delimbiyr south of Waterdeep. The settlement has stood for nearly 400 years and now consists of about 40 stone buildings and a castle, all protected by a high stone wall.

The town of Daggerford gets its name from a historic altercation between a merchant's son and a lizardfolk raiding party. The young man, armed only with a dagger, stood in the middle of the ford and held off the lizardfolk until reinforcements could arrive.

The Greatshouts are the ruling family of Daggerford with Duke Pwyll Greatshout being the town's current leader. The Greatshouts have ruled Daggerford for five generations, dating back to the first Duke, Rugyar the Just.

Daggerford is viewed by many as a backwater, especially when compared to Waterdeep, the town's nearest neighbor. It is not uncommon for Waterdhavian criminals and corrupt politicians to set up temporary roots in Daggerford, until their troubles in Waterdeep blow over. For this reason, Daggerford's population is more diverse and cultured than the typical agrarian town along the Trade Way.

Illefarn

Hear ye all my tale of woe,
About the land called Illefarn,
Which bordered on the elven lands,
And sheltered all from pain and harm.

Welcoming was the elven lord,
And gracious was his lady fair,
With gates set wide to visiting kings,
And pleasantries exchanged without a care.

Then came humans on shining mounts,
To hoe and farm the blackened soil,
Met kindly by elves and dwarves alike,
They reaped the bounty of endless toil.

But kinship was lost to orcish hordes,
Come down from the north with axe and shield,
Who destroyed the ranks of elves and dwarves,
And slew all humans too brave to yield.

Now but a shadow of its former glory,
Wondrous Illefarn has fallen away,
But lest ye lose hope of great Illefarn's revival,
Know that we dwarves will yet have our day.

Eye Scream

Ingredients:

2 tbsp. eye of newt
2 cups swamp water (brackish)
1/2 cup blueberries
3 cups Gorgon's milk (substitute cow's milk if Gorgon's is not available)
1 cup good intentions (or other sugary sweetener)

Directions:

1. In a medium bronze cauldron, reduce eye of newt, blueberries, and swamp water to a sludge-like consistency.
2. Over a low fire, slowly mix in good intentions while stirring vigorously with a holly branch so mixture doesn't burn.
3. Remove cauldron from heat and slowly stir in milk. 
4. Cast a Ray of Frost spell on the cauldron and serve!

Beware the Lizard Marsh!
Another expeditionary tale of infamous Sword Coast locales, by Emythene Faldree and her renowned group of crack adventurers.
* * *

This time, dear readers, we shall be exploring the Lizard Marsh to the west of the town of Daggerford, just along the coast. Historically an unpleasant place, the Lizardfolk within the marsh have always been an ever-present threat to Daggerford, the Trade Way traffic, and not to mention the local farmers themselves. The name Daggerford is in fact derived from a boy who wielded a mere dagger to defend himself against a score of Lizardfolk on the banks of the River Delimbiyr several centuries ago. But the mysteries of the marsh have remained largely undiscovered since that time. So let us proceed and see exactly what secrets the Lizard Marsh holds...
- Emythene Faldree

Day 3. The dark branches seem to reach at us like clawed hands as we trekked through the quagmire of the marsh, with the mud sucking at our boots. After our initial encounter with the feral tribal Lizardfolk, our show of force seems to have dissuaded them from continued probing of our defenses. Our tracker guide insists though that they are shadowing our progress, and he can constantly be seen staring into the dark green waters after the elusive creatures.

Day 4. We have been lucky. A black dragon, obviously quite young judging from its size, took us by surprise today. It burst from the trees with such ferocity that it made quick work of one of our porters before we could move to defend ourselves. The creature did not escape with its prize, however, as our arrows had feathered it before it could take many steps back towards its refuge. We pried out its razor-sharp teeth as souvenirs, for how many can claim to have slain a dragon!

Day 6. We have lost Durns. A snake so small as to be beneath notice has turned out to be highly poisonous. Durns' joviality will be missed around the nightly fires.

Day 7. We have been faced with several attacks from the Lizardfolk and these assaults have not left us unscathed. Three of our guards now lie dead, including dear Ignatious. I am beginning to believe that these attacks are only meant to wear us down and not true offensives. The marsh itself wears on our morale as well.

Day 9. It looked as if the Lizardfolk had finally decided to leave us be, disappearing completely into the foliage, but the reason became clear before long. In a brackish pond along which we made camp, we encountered a beast undoubtedly related to the common turtle found in many creeks. Yet the size and viciousness of this beast was of a completely different scale. Four members of our group are dead or dying from wounds caused by its huge snapping jaws after they strolled along the pond's edge. I am loath to leave behind the prize of its shell, which is a full 14 feet across and thick enough to stop arrows. Instead, its massive head is the prize I shall return with.

Day 10. A dark form in the night took the last porter. Sharp claws riding upon leathery wings by the sole account of it. I am forced to abandon my prize as only four of us remain.

Day 11. Our guide has abandoned us. Curse him!

Day 12. Maltan, Kegrunt, and I have decided that our expedition is unfortunately at an end. We shall navigate back towards Daggerford using the sun by day and the stars by night, just as we did when we became lost at sea in search of the Isle of Mysts. Although we leave this adventure behind us, we shall live to see another day and more adventures along the Sword Coast! We may not have uncovered all the mysteries within the marsh, but we have confirmed that its dangers are quite vicious, and that it is indeed a most inhospitable place. To all those who would dare to venture here, all I can counsel is this: beware the Lizard Marsh!

Poor Man's Soup

Ingredients:

1 normal-length hemp rope
1 small sack
2 burly thugs
1 blackjack
1 bucket of cold water
1 diplomatic thug

Directions:

1. At dusk, take the rope, sack, blackjack, and three thugs to a good-aligned church.
2. Creep stealthily up on the priest during their solitary evening prayer.
3. Conk the priest on the back of the head with the blackjack, tie them up, and place the sack over their head.
4. Move the priest to some discreet location suitable for dining.
5. Awaken the priest with the bucket of cold water. 
6. Have the diplomatic thug explain to the priest that their release from bondage is contingent on the casting of a Create Food and Water spell.
7. To show there's no hard feelings, invite the priest to dinner.

Stinky Beef Stew

Ingredients:

1 dead cow plus entrails
1 bunch black mold
1 handful mushrooms
7 pints beer
7 pints scrumpy cider
Some kind of thorny bush

Directions:

1. Chop up dead cow in four pieces.
2. Wrap some entrails around each cow piece and fasten tight with toothpick.
3. Hold cow piece over fire until eyes water from stink.
4. Chop up burnt cow and entrails and put bits in pot.
5. Drink one pint of beer and pour one pint of scrumpy cider into pot. Do this until all beer and cider is gone.
6. Put pot on fire.
7. Drop in mold, mushrooms, and thorny bush.
8. Cook until stew so burnt it stink up kitchen.
9. Serve with lemon wedge and sprig of parsley.

Trade Way Travel Stops: A Visitor's Guide to the Trade Way South of Daggerford

So, you've seen all there is to see of the quaint, country town known as Daggerford and are at a loss for what to do next. Well, my friends, the Trade Way area south of Daggerford is an area literally brimming with the promise of new adventures.

Leaving Daggerford by its Caravan Gate and heading south for half a day, your first stop is Gillian's Hill, a charming hamlet that once served as the center of law enforcement along this stretch of the Trade Way. Today, the small outpost serves as a minor trading hub and includes an excellent curiosity shop known as Torleth's Treasures. Other places of note include the historical Gillian's Hill Cemetery and the famed Gillian's Tower that served as a lookout post for the hamlet's namesake and former ranger-protector, Gillian Cantilar.

Another half-day's journey past Gillian's Hill lies Liam's Hold. This is a fine place to book a room for the night. Although the hamlet lies not far from the treacherous Trollbark Forest, the area is well-protected (for the most part), and the Holdfast Inn offers soft beds and lively conversation. You may find some of the Liam's Hold locals to be a tad superstitious, but this only serves to heighten the burg's old-world, agrarian atmosphere.

South of Liam's Hold, it is best to hire onto a caravan, as much for your protection as theirs...
This key was found on the body of Captain Dratharion, the head of the Griffons Mercenary Company.

These cloaks were created by the united elven tribes of the Fallen Kingdom that once flourished where Laughing Hollow now stands. These were bestowed as honored gifts to the esteemed nobility of the allied dwarven and elven clans. Very few of these relics have survived to this day.

Although somewhat damaged from misuse by an ogre king, this solid gold cup retains much of its value. It likely graced the table of a high lord in some day long past, although any form of identifiable heraldry is no longer discernible.
This golden goblet is encrusted with several small gemstones. It likely belonged to one of the kings of the dwarven realm of Illefarn. This glittering treasure is a thief's dream come true...
This wand will make all locations in the world map visible.

This circular mirror seems quite old, yet it still gleams. The highly reflective, well-polished, metallic surface is slightly concave, as if it were intended to focus light in a specific direction. The circular base is quite solid, as if the mirror was designed to be placed on some sort of stand...

This stone bears a divine enchantment from Moradin 'The Soulforger,' granting exceptional abilities to dwarven craftsmen when they toil near this artifact. The invocation of such a blessing is obscured in dwarven lore, therefore these stones are very rare. In fact, they are said to be an earthly manifestation of Moradin's divine power, and not bestowed frivolously.

This weapon was forged for the ancient dwarf king of Illefarn, Rurin Peakgrinder III. It bears the stamp of a master dwarven weaponsmith of the Ironeater clan. Legend says the weapon was used to destroy a tribe of ogre mages, and it was buried with the king when he died out of fear of a lingering ogre curse.
This weapon appears to be the work of a master dwarven smith.

This appears to be a chain of several bones from various creatures. Bits of old, dried flesh are still attached to some of the bones. This was the charm of the gnoll shaman, Rattlefang, and it can be used to summon a dreadful disease upon one's enemies.
This appears to be a chain of several bones from various creatures. Bits of old, dried flesh are still attached to some of the bones.

This heavy axe appears to be made entirely of stone, certainly hewn by a master dwarven craftsman. Although the workmanship is extraordinary, it must be some sort of decorative object rather than a functional weapon.

This torque is a symbol of dwarven nobility and honor. Forged from mithril and decorated with powerful runes of earth and war, this would have been a symbol of great status among the ancient dwarves of Illefarn, where this item was found.
This torque was found buried in a dwarven tomb in Illefarn.

Who knows where the creature that murdered Vejoni attained this item. The material is strangely cool to the touch and difficult to look at -- it seems to shift and reform beneath your very gaze!

Whatever the background, it is clear that the blade is powerful, and through some unknown planar power source is able to summon a horde of alien tentacled creatures, distort vision around a chosen individual to protect them from ranged attacks, and either bind or summon an alien creature to this plane of existence.

Following Vejoni's demise, these powers are waning as the planar connection weakens, and will not be renewed once all charges have been expended.

Amnwater No.1 hails from the town of Amnwater, a former roadside tavern in Amn that grew to become a major stop for caravan traders.

The presence of this beer as the guest offering at the Holdfast Inn is rather synchronous with Matagar Bugo's plans for Daggerford.
A delicious pastry case stuffed with mincemeat and dried fruits. Just the thing for a chilly evening with a glass of mulled wine.
Warm, moist buttery pastry surrounds a luxuriant center of succulent red and black cherries poached in elderflower wine with a little sugar. Just... divine.

This large multifaceted gem contains a horrifying truth. Trapped inside in a miniature pocket universe is the soul and essence of your great friend Talerenne! You have no idea how you might set about freeing her.

The sight of a tiny Talerenne is both saddening and unnerving, and you constantly move the pristine prison through your fingers as if to reassure her of your presence.

Some years before Xanda married her husband Michael, she was courted by a middle-aged wizard hailing from Cormyr called Dwenthor of the Winds.

Xanda was young and Dwenthor wise in the ways of the world, and she soon fell under his spell, although there was no actual magic involved. Dwenthor lived several miles from Liam's Hold in an old stone house now used by shepherds, and he enchanted this cape so that Xanda could travel safely through the snow and winds of a harsh Sword Coast winter. Additionally, the wearer gains the ability to persuade even the most determined to their way of thinking, a feature Dwenthor included so Xanda might tell him that he was the bravest wizard the realms had ever seen, and that he himself might believe her. In reality, he was a complete coward, and their romance ended when a team of mercenaries arrived to return him to Cormyr and serve his time in the War Wizards. To this day, Xanda has never heard from him again.
Clearly this is the missing component from Evani's Incredible Fantabulizer. A precise understanding of its functioning would take years to achieve.

The Bakadi Brothers, Jemzo and Jamzo, were two of the finest thieves ever to emerge from the sweltering streets of Memnon in faraway Calimshan. Their bravery and cunning were the stuff of legend even within their own lifetimes, and they rose rapidly to head one of the infamous crime cartels of their homeland.

It was said that "no job was too big, no vault too well protected, and no maiden able to resist" the power of the Bakadi brothers, but it seems that this was somewhat of an exaggeration. A little over 400 years ago they left their homes, telling trusted lieutenants they were 'heading out for the greatest heist of all time'. They were never seen again.

The presence of their remains here suggest that the aforesaid 'heist' involved the treasures of the wizard and warrior Sundar Halyndliam, and clearly they were unsuccessful. Exactly what he did with them upon their capture is unclear, but their skulls are now potent in magic, and clearly have been tampered with by someone with great knowledge of the arcane.

Teygan has carefully written down the directions for reaching the Zhentarim caravan travelling under the banner of the Iron Throne.

In order to reach it, leave the Brush of Barbs in a westerly direction and when the path forks after a couple of miles, follow the caravan tracks heading north-east.

This incredibly ancient object was created by a priestess of the Goddess Mystryl as a gift to the church of Jannath after they provided assistance in the creation of new earth-related spells. The priestess, who also went by the name of Dreamstone, created this incarnation of the earth's nurturing and destructive powers to protect her new allies from all who might do them harm.

It is rumored that the priestess Dreamstone also wove into this item the power for two beings to communicate during their sleeping hours through dream imagery and symbolism, but it is unclear if this is true, or how such an effect might be created.

A hand sized piece of stone bearing a curious glyph that has been half worn away. The stone itself is curiously warm to the touch, and its texture bears none of the harshness one might usually associate with rough cut rock.

A crude hand has written in basic common:

"Keep weapons coming - need much more. Make orcs understand to be more careful when travelling into forest. Don't mean trolls, mean cursed nosey adventurers. Found one sniffing around waterfall near cave entrance. He won't be sniffing no more without nose HA HA HA! He also got no more eyes now just to be sure. Now we send him to you for pens. Make sure Herab gets him and the others you have caught in payment for weapons.

"The Master will be most unhappy if orcs be followed again - you know what that means!
Evidence Found in the Smugglers' Cave

This fruity, and somewhat flat brew is named after the Elfsong Tavern in Baldur's Gate where it was first served by the current owner, "Lady" Alyth Elendara.

The Tavern itself is famed for an unusual haunting, a ghostly female voice that is heard from time to time throughout the establishment, and the stuffed baby beholder that hangs over the bar. Certainly these features are of more interest than this distinctly average cider!

One of the earlier creations of the infamous inventor and performer known only as Evani, this item is actually one of practical use rather than pure artistic design.

Evani herself is a rather colorful character both in dress and attitude and this ring literally embodies these traits! A little garish to look at perhaps, but useful to adventurers in a pinch without doubt.

You stole this cloak from Falias Emberthumb when his back was turned. A label stitched neatly into the hem reads "Property of F. Emberthumb Esq. If found, please return to W., D., & F. Emberthumb Tailors, 234 Turmish Way, Waterdeep."

The cloak holds a limited number of charges that allow the wearer to become invisible, although taking any kind of hostile action will break the protection. The perfect thing for a merchant travelling along dangerous roads.

You stole this cloak from Falias Emberthumb when his back was turned. A label stitched neatly into the hem reads "Property of F. Emberthumb Esq. If found, please return to W., D., & F. Emberthumb Tailors, 234 Turmish Way, Waterdeep."

This seems to be what passes for instructions in orc culture:

"Stupid thick-skull it be simple! From forest head north all the way to the human farms. Scout meet you there and take rest of way.

"Think your mother gave too much boiled slug when you baby, made you into slugbrain so say this again - travel ONLY at night, DO NOT attack farmers or anyone else! There will be time for that later when the Master is ready.

This fiery liquid is reputed to be distilled from the blood of the legendary phoenix. Whether or not this is true, it is a highly potent and sought after elixir, with just a sip being enough to protect the imbiber from extremes of temperature while erecting a protective shield around the drinker's body.

This short but sharp blade has peeled and sliced so much garlic that its edge has become burning to exposed skin.

The smell does tend to be a little off-putting though...
This is a silver crescent moon and harp pin worn by members of the Harpers as a means of identification.

Pried from the fingers of its previous owner this light blade is typical of the type used by trusted Zhent officers. Every time it draws blood the wielder absorbs a portion of the victim's life energy.

Blades such as this make for terrifying instruments of torture. Some owners have been known to become addicted to the daily drawing of blood from prisoners, slaves and other unfortunates, keeping them just alive in order to provide a ready source of replenishment.
This key grants access to the upper floor of the Holdfast Inn in Liam's Hold.

You have written some notes on a napkin to allow you to recreate the garlic ice cream invented by Rab Bitnez (and somehow, you wonder why you even wrote this down. Oh well, nevermind).

INGREDIENTS:

4 eggs
9oz sugar
lots of cream!
a pinch of salt
6 cloves garlic

This is a dead easy ice cream recipe -- you don't have to make a custard or anything! Well, actually if you aren't a wizard, sorcerer or white dragon it does get tricky in one place...

Beat the egg whites and the sugar together to form stiff peaks. Whip the cream until thick and fold into the whites/sugar mix gently.

Using the flat of a kitchen knife or a fork mash the garlic and sugar together, then beat the garlic pulp into the egg yolks, and stir into the cream meringue mixture.

Now for the tricky bit. Angle the bowl such that you can easily fire your frost ray spell into the mixture without any slipping out. Note: use of ice storm is NOT recommended, as the resulting kitchen damage can spoil the enjoyment of this otherwise heavenly dessert. Rogues and bards may like to make use of their use magic device talents at this point and borrow a frost ray wand from a friendly neighborhood spellcaster. Failing that, leaving the mixture outside for a few hours has been known to work... if you live in Icewind Dale... and it's not summer.

Allow to soften slightly before serving.
A lengthy note written in an alpha-numeric code. Despite being unreadable this is clearly the correspondence that Teygan wishes you to recover.
A set of orders and other information written in code. Despite being unintelligible without a code book, this is clearly the document that Teygan wishes you to steal.
An oak barrel filled with creamy brown ale. There should be plenty in there for a good party!

Iylliana Pryde was an elven rogue renowned for her incredible agility, love of a stand up fight, and slightly wayward sense of battle strategy (that is to say a seemingly limitless capacity to charge into the fray and worry about who's doing the resurrecting later!). 
Somehow, incredibly, she managed to achieve a fine old age even for an elf, and as she relaxed at home spending the days chatting with old friends she decided to pass on the equipment that she had had made for her to her heir apparent, another young rogue going by the pseudonym "Alchemy". Many years later "Alchemy" fell on hard times (it is rumoured after a romantic encounter with a flame haired musician with a jealous partner) and sold this catsuit to Torleth in order to raise funds. No one knows what became of the feline ears that Iylliana insists used to accompany the garment...

The author of this communication is clearly unhappy:

"The Master commands we put an end to the goblin's stupidity. Their thieving ways may ruin everything. The human farmers have even offered a reward to any heroes that help them out.

"Proceed to their caves and kill half a dozen of them to make an example. Be as brutal as you like...

"When you are done gather a troop together and burn away the trolls that are massing at the great rock outcropping. They are beginning to disrupt the flow of weapons from the drop off cave.

"Do not return until you have carried out these orders unless you want an eye burned out!

The deranged Netherese jockstrap manufacturer Kulvin Clank often took things too literally, and this was just the case when he created this oddity.

Kulvin was a firm believer in the adage "keep your enemies where you can see them" and, he reasoned, there was no safer nor nearer place than just below the belt. With the zeal of a man under the spell of a great revelation he set about the creation of a powerful set of undergarments with the idea of imprisoning his enemies in tiny sequins which he would then keep forever under his trousers.

Sadly for Kulvin to trap his enemies was not enough, and he met an untimely death when crushed under a falling statue of the goddess Tyche, Queen of the Accidental. The ebbing effigy damaged many of the sequins, freeing their cursing contents in front of a crowd of unsuspecting onlookers who were rather taken a back to see almost a dozen high powered wizards all suddenly appear, the majority of them incandescent with righteous anger and frustration.

Certainly this garment has lost the most of its power, but there remains yet one sequin hanging by a couple of threads, and whatever is imprisoned withing would no doubt be most grateful for its freedom...
An exceedingly well fitting matching set of vest and underwear offering excellent support without any sacrifices to comfort.
Culvin Klank's Matching Vest and Jockstrap of Containment

Lashar always keeps one eye open for beautiful artifacts such as this one and regularly sources exotic items with unique designs. This sword was made for a holy ruler of a desert kingdom far away to the East.

The death of the creature Metastakixx still ways heavily on your heart and you will never forget the lament that you sung in the House of Mists. How these pipes came to be in your possession is a mystery, but the haunting melody of that song sounds as close to perfection as you can imagine when played on them.
This supple chainmail armor has been blessed by clerics of Lliira and can call on that divinity's grace one time per day.
A beautiful cloak that appeared in your possession after the death of the creature Metastakixx, an apparent reward for your freeing the creature from its eons of bondage.
Quite possibly the most ornate and ancient looking key you have ever seen!
This armor has been blackened during the process of forging the mail, and is surprisingly well fashioned by orcish standards.
This meat will soon become inedible.
A fiery, bitter and evil brew, and of that there is no doubt!
A large helm for an orcish head.
This spear has been finished off with a cruelly barbed head atop the wooden shaft.
This long flat blade has the look and feel of a typical longsword.

You have written some notes on a napkin to allow you to recreate the garlic pavlova invented by Rab Bitnez (and somehow, you wonder why you even wrote this down. Oh well, nevermind).

INGREDIENTS:

5 egg whites
salt (just a pinch!)
9oz sugar
1 teaspoon vinegar
1/2 teaspoon vanilla essence
2 teaspoons corn starch
10 cloves garlic (plus more to decorate!)
cream

Beat the whites of the eggs with the salt and vinegar until stiff peaks form. Gradually add the sugar, half of the garlic finely chopped, and vanilla until a thick mixture forms, then gently beat in the corn starch.

Pile the mixture into circular shapes on a greased baking tray, with a circular depression in the middle of each for filling later. Note: the mixture will swell during cooking!

Bake gently for 1 1/2 hours. Allow to cool.

Whip the cream and the remaining finely chopped garlic and fill the depressions in the now crispy garlic meringue shells, and serve immediately!

You have written some notes on a napkin to allow you to recreate the garlic pie invented by Rab Bitnez (and somehow, you wonder why you even wrote this down. Oh well, nevermind).

INGREDIENTS:

10 whole bulbs of garlic
8 sheets of filo pastry (from Nell's shop...)
goat's cheese
butter
a little fresh parsley (any kind will do)

Roast the whole garlic bulbs for 45 minutes, and allow to cool before peeling. Mash all of the peeled cloves with salt and pepper to taste, and some fresh parsley (to take the edge off things...)

Crumble the goat's cheese into the garlic mash.

Melt the butter and line a pie dish with half of the pastry, brushing with butter between each sheet. Pour the garlic and cheese mixture into the dish, and top with the remaining pastry sheets, brushing each with butter once again. Bake the pie for 40 minutes in a medium heat, and serve either warm or cold. Fantastic!

A collection of hilarious songs written by the infamous bard-mage best known by her pseudonym of 'Prankster'. The lyrics are classic comedy, having caused audiences the length of the Sword Coast to collapse into fits of uncontrollable laughter on numerous occasions. A little laughter goes a long way, sharpening the mind, but over exposure and too much hilarity can lead to painful experiences!

Most of the Prankster's best known tunes are here, including the hilarious "Ruby, don't take your beholder to town", the avant garde strangeness of "Rust Monster!" (It wasn't just rust, it was a Rust Monster!), the charming ode to friendship of "Me, my kobold, and I", and many, many more...
This seems to be a collection of songs as evidenced by the presence of musical scores and sets of lyrics on alternate pages. Something about them is quite incomprehensible though.
The metal of this key is strangely warm to the touch.
Vejoni has discovered this robe on one of his planar travels. There is no information regarding it's maker or their location.

This blade was taken from the hand of some ancient form of shadow creature. There is something altogether unpleasant about it, as if something watches you from a great distance, something that bears great malice towards all life.

Nothing and no one are quite what they appear to be!

The wearer of Edge of Uncertainty is blessed/cursed with the ability to mutate their body into other forms, and causes other creatures to become uncertain as to the wearer's motives and desires making them more inclined to believe whatever the wearer says.

Try it on and see!
This leather armor is incredibly well made, and reinforced with a light and flexible metal plates. It is enchanted and provides considerable extra protection to the wearer.
This is the signet ring of the Greatshout family. You should keep hold of it in case anyone questions your intent as it will prove that you are speaking for the Duke and his sister.

This gently curved blade is highly unusual in that it has been enchanted by a bard rather than a wizard. The identity of the creator is unknown, but whoever it was created a weapon that sings a gentle lilting song that is only heard by the welder. Rather than distract the user, however, this song aids relaxation and focus in the heat of battle.

Shake and snap!

The instructions seem simple enough -- according to the manufacturer this glass (?) tube contains captured starlight...
This key opens the doors of the Temple structure on the edge of Liam's Hold.
The act of firing these bolts causes them to heat up and cause additional searing damage to their target.

You pathetic failure, letting that mealy-mouthed, platitudinous prig of a Harper talk you around. I would love to say it was fun while it lasted but I do not wish to encourage you to egotism! Well, I must be leaving you. My presence here can be explained by my searching for the whereabouts of my love Ashemmi, and I have learnt something most encouraging and must depart. Strange isn't it? You would call me evil and yet I act purely out of concern for another. Enjoy puzzling that one over while I get on with more important matters.

Give my regards to Drelia. I am sure she will be most grateful...

Until another day then,

Sememmon.
A plump juicy apple covered in honey and skewered on a wooden stick so as the eater doesn't get sticky fingers. Warning - do NOT attempt to talk and eat at the same time!
This is the key to Torleth's underground strongroom.

The Amulet of Konash has a history of cropping up in places where great evils come to pass. It is not known if the item itself is cursed, and its origins are shrouded in mystery. Some claim it belonged to the lieutenant of some ancient evil God, while others tell of its reputed origins deep in the Underdark, but no one knows for sure.

The Staff of Konash has a history of cropping up in places where great evils come to pass. It is not known if the item itself is cursed, and its origins are shrouded in mystery. Some claim it was the weapon of choice for some ancient evil God's lieutenant, while others tell of its reputed origins deep in the Underdark, but no one knows for sure.

Taken from the desiccated hand of the vampire priest of Vaheraun called Sieronius Dethick, this ring once symbolized the bond between Dethick and his original wife who passed away long ago. Sieronius had planned to call on the cursed power of his deity and forge a new marriage with an innocent in order to escape his prison.

When Edwin Daggerford defeated the devil Gorgomorz, a number of magical items were produced in the aftermath of battle to honor the victory, and prepare for the future.

This potion grants the drinker an increase to Charisma to inspire their leadership, heals minor wounds, and boosts their courage to counteract the terror the mere sight of a mighty devil brings.

During the fierce Goblin Wars of the Misty Forest, Endervale Hunt, a local trapper, was instrumental in turning the tide in the Battle of Steepwood Gorge. He arrived to the aid of the local wood elves with a force of hillmen trappers, who until that point had been feuding with the elves over land encroachment. In gratitude for this aid, Endervale was given this suit of magical armor. Unfortunately, before the end of the Goblin Wars, Endervale fell in an ambush and the armor was lost.

The origins of these clothes are a mystery. They first appeared as tattered rags worn by a coinless vagabond. The beggar wore the outfit for many years, until one day he was set upon by a group of unruly bandits looking to slay the man for sport. The bandits were unhappy to learn of the armor's true nature as they set about trying to extinguish themselves in a nearby brook. As the story of this event spread, many beggars in the area began donning red rags of their own to frighten off would-be attackers. Although this trend has since subsided, many ruffians still take care when approaching a beggar dressed all in red.

This flexible armor was designed to suit the fighting style of a duelist, as well as handle the rolling deck of a ship at sea. Valued by brigands along the Sword Coast, the armor was once paid out as ransom to the pirate Baralen the Black for the safe return of Lord Tygarian's daughter. However, after receiving the armor, the pirate chose not to return the young woman to her father. Upon hearing the news, she flew into a rage, struck Baralen down in his cabin and made off with the armor, which she used to help jump-start her own piratical career.

This suit of chainmail was created by a coven of witches, known as the Newts' Brood, who gave the armor to their ranger-lover, Tholan the Beautiful. The witches used the armor to keep track of Tholan, who possessed an unending wanderlust that caused him to travel for months on end.

Legend claims that when Tholan finally wed a lovely elven maid, he was forced to discard the armor so that he might evade retribution from his former lovers. The armor resurfaced much later in the care of a self-styled (and undoubtedly short-lived) kobold hero named Muurg.

And it was said that a solar of Tyr descended and spoke unto Kishal, bequeathing her a mighty gift of a brilliant suit of golden chain: "You shall fear not the darkness, for you are bathed in Tyr's own light. You shall fear not the minions of darkness, for on you they shall have no hold. Go forth unto the darkness, as it is his will to spread the way of justice. And to those who have been wronged and are powerless to defend themselves, you shall deliver vengeance upon their guilty aggressors."

Lord Francis Tenraw commissioned this suit of armor in anticipation of a war that never came. The suit served him well in a ceremonial fashion, until his death (of old age). His daughter, who did not see the use of ceremony, sold the armor to finance a library.

"A wise wizard always plans a retreat." Such was the motto of a now forgotten wizard who created this robe. Although it is widely accepted that the original owner lived a long and largely danger-free life, she also never achieved greatness by avoiding danger. 

The robe has made many appearances in a wide area of Faerûn, including an overzealous monk from Athkatla who insisted on using the robe to charge into danger (deceased), and as the prized possession of a skittish noble in Saelmur, who was known to wear out the soles of his shoes from always pacing to and fro worrying.

Leustrarax, shaman of the Bear-Tooth tribe, took this enchanted suit of armor as a trophy from a knight who tried unsuccessfully to expand his fiefdom into Bear-Tooth territory. Not long after the altercation with the knight, the shaman's village was attacked by a fearsome band of orcs, known as the Bloody Tusk clan. After beating back a series of relentless attacks from the orcs, Leustrarax and the tribe went on the offensive, tracking the retreating orcs back to a large cave. Donning the armor, which provided him with the ability to see in the dark, Leustrarax was able to locate the orc chieftain's lair and slay the creature with a single, poison-tipped arrow. Years later, the armor was lost during an unsuccessful raid of a well-defended caravan heading south.

A young man, known as Alatian, was apprenticed to the lich, Estera. Alatian served as Estera's gopher, retrieving things from the lands of the living to further the lich's research and experiments. Estera gave Alatian this cloak so the young man might never come under a spell that might be used to reveal the lich's whereabouts.

Alatian's constant trips through the local graveyards gave rise to ghost stories, since the cloak gave off a faint, bluish glow. Alatian wore the cloak for many years until one day attaining his own "second life" as a lich.

Amian Niast, a prominent Waterdhavian merchant, commissioned seven of these robes for her elite guard. Under her command, the Seven Scourges became feared among the lesser merchants competing for business around Waterdeep. Eventually tiring of their mistress' brutish tactics, five of the seven enacted a coup to take over Amian's business. During the ensuing conflict, they slew Amian, her son, and two of their former Scourge comrades.

This armor was made by the druid, Yensila, from the hide of a legendary bear that protected her grove. The armor's sole purpose was to allow Yensila to seek vengeance for the bear's death at the hands of a pair of ruthless poachers. While hunting the poachers, Yensila's grove fell into ruin and became a twisted, haunted place. However, once Yensila's task was completed, the grove instantly sprang back to life, as if paid a visit by the bear's noble spirit.

Tempered with the fire of a red dragon's breath and bathed in the blood of sacrificed children, this suit of armor can only be worn by someone whose lust for power far outweighs their empathy for others. As such, this armor has had no shortage of users.
These small white berries have a delicate pale skin and a slightly minty taste.
These small white berries have a delicate pale skin and a slightly minty taste.

We the faithful must remain true to Umgatlik. All effort must be made to ensure his return and all hardships will be rewarded upon his return. The world is to be made ready for his triumphant return. Join our voices in prayer.

Our lord Umgatlik, who shall rise again.
From whom blessing and greatness flow.
In his image that we might strive to become.
All praise be to Umgatlik. May he hear our calls.
To the day where Umgatlik is to be reborn into this world we wait.
Until that day, while our enemies fester, we wait and grow in strength.
Until that day when our enemies will fall before us.
Our hidden legions will rise and he will lead us into a new age.
All praise be to Umgatlik.
All glory be to the age of Umgatlik.

Duke Greatshout, esteemed leader of Daggerford, presented you with this shining medal as a reward for saving the town from a vengeful baatezu devil named Gorgomorz. From this day forward, legends of your valiant actions in Daggerford will spread among the outsiders, who have begun to whisper your name quietly, almost fearfully. You can use the Duke's medal to inspire your comrades in battle, and to strike fear into the heart of any outsider who dares to challenge you in combat.
These bones, from some unfortunate humanoid, are not yellowed by age.
These blue woolen tunics, decorated with Helm's emblem, are common among the good people of Hluthvar, the Helmite stronghold city near Darkhold.
This sword, owned by Raegen Brunegar, was blessed by Helm himself. This was a rare gift indeed, with the weapon being imbued with powers against undead.
These black dragon eggs were given to you by Redeye, self-proclaimed leader of the lizardfolk tribes.
You found this heavy brass key hidden in Feldran Exeltis' study.

This short letter is addressed to Feldran Exeltis:

Lord Feldran, 
Our esteemed agency has received your request to locate the mysterious Kingdom of Fanloc, and to determine its total wealth. If the Kingdom of Fanloc exists anywhere in the known Realms, we shall locate it soon. Further correspondence shall follow.

The letter is signed by an employee of "The Agency of Cartographic Investigations, Waterdeep branch."
This large stick of wood is banded with rows of sharp metal studs. Bhaal's holy symbol, a skull surrounded by a circle of blood droplets, has been etched into the wood by a strong acid.
This black hammer head is long and curved, with a sharp point at one end. Although the made from strong bone, you can see rows of tiny lines, made from some kind of acid, etched into the head.
This misshapen chunk of cold iron glows faintly, and feels warm to the touch.
This thick wooden stick glows faintly, and feels warm to the touch.
This long thin metal band is covered with a thin glaze of freezing ice.
Twisted and broken, this long metal blade is covered with a thick layer of freezing ice.

Oh Great and Mighty Gorgomorz, lord of all ... alliance between our organization and your mighty armies ... the Black Network will prosper when Daggerford is crushed by our combined might ... Our bandit raiders, operating from a hidden stronghold in the region, are already sowing the seeds of Daggerford's certain destruction ... Oh Great and Mighty Gorgomorz, most fearsome of all devils, your victory shall be legendary, and all mortals shall tremble when they hear your footsteps!

-- Fzoul

Effigies such as this one are commonly used in black magic rituals to gain power over another creature. A personal item is required to begin the ritual. This particular effigy, a small rag doll, has a few strands of greasy black hair tied to the top of its head.

A Chultan witchdoctor, named Intulik of the Blood, created this helm by fusing together the spirits of seventeen tigers and binding them to the helm's metallic structure. The helm's powers aided the witchdoctor in the slaying of numerous political rivals and the eventual subjugation of the Chultan people.

Intulik would have ruled for decades had she not been killed by the renowned bounty hunter, Tatchalik, who took the helm as payment for ending Intulik's career and life. Tatchalik was last seen heading for Waterdeep with the helm on display for all to see.

A wise king had this crown commissioned when he rightly surmised that his advisors were plotting against him. Secretly substituting this crown for the one attained at his coronation, he eventually was able to discover and capture the treasonous aides. This eventually led the "fake" crown to supplant the original as the symbol of rulership.

It is ironic, then, how a traveling bard managed to return the original crown to its rightful place. Sneaking about the castle the night before her performance, the bard managed to swap crowns, placing the fake in the castle vault and the original on the king's nightstand. The next night, after giving the performance of her life, the bard was told she could claim whatever she liked from the king's treasury. She claimed the crown from the vault for her own, unbeknownst to all as being the fake, and was never seen again...

Artimal Penfall, the dwarven scribe who wore this helmet (and whose given name was actually Angus Hammerfall), was a dedicated scholar. On numerous voyages by land or by sea, he was often seen writing about the events of a battle while it raged on all around him. Though an accomplished war correspondent, Artimal is perhaps best known for penning the seminal comedic work entitled "My Dinner with Goblins," that Volo the bard once called "the funniest thing in print."
This heart was cut from the corpse of a small bird.

This gruesome bag is made from large patches of dried skin haphazardly stitched together with dark black thread. The patches are of many different colors and textures because each patch of skin was cut from the living flesh of a different creature: human, elf, gnome, halfling, and dwarf.

These sharp knives, called Bloodletters, were once used by priests of Bhaal when preparing blood sacrifices to their evil god. The poison contained in the blade subdued the victim long enough for the blood sacrifice to proceed without any unfortunate distractions.
When you slay a humanoid, its blood will be collected into this empty bottle. After you have filled 10 bottles of blood, you should return to Xatuum in the temple of Bhaal.
This bottle contains the blood of a humanoid creature that you killed. After you have filled 10 bottles of blood, you should return to Xatuum in the temple of Bhaal.
A druid named Tatham, who was polymorphed into a seagull, claims that the magic contained within this bloodstone can lift the "fowl" curse that afflicts him.

A poor shepherd named Lavna gave you this small charm as a reward for slaying the dreaded One-Eyed Worg of the Wild Pastures. The charm is shaped like a small lens, and will allow you to see what might be hidden in the darkness.
This bloody heart was cut from the corpse of a large and very unfriendly devil named Abatorru.
Elwinster's Oil: Squeaky Wheel Salve. Guaranteed to turn those wheels without a squeak or I shall eat my hat! (hamster wheels excluded)
This heavy canvas sack is filled with dark black soil.

Exeltis ice wine, one of the finest vintages in the Realms, is made from the small gray grapes that grow along the base of the Blade Cliffs. In recent years, Exeltis wine has become scarce, greatly increasing its value.
This key opens most of the doors in Castle Exeltis.

During the final days of Illefarn, when orcs and dwarves waged fearsome battles deep underground, the fabled dwarven warrior Goladrin struggled to defend a sacred shrine. After fighting tirelessly for seven days and seven nights, Goladrin fell, mortally wounded, with his silver battlehorn at his side. Since the shrine had been a sacred place before it was defiled, the horn became magically imbued with Goladrin's valiant spirit. Whenever the horn is blown, Goladrin's spirit will aid you in combat.
This silver horn is covered with dwarven runes.

"The Golden Book"
By Matagar Bugo

Daggerford should be a prosperous town! With the east-west trade from the River Delimbiyr and the north-south trade from the Trade Way, it is a town that should be destined for greatness. However, throughout its long history, Daggerford has been in the care of leaders who lacked vision. They saw the town as a quaint stop-off for local farmers to come peddle their wares. They ignored its potential of becoming the next great coastal merchant center to rival Waterdeep and Baldur's Gate. Well, Daggerford's new leadership is about to change all that!

The naysayers amongst you will proclaim that our town lacks a navy to protect merchant vessels from river and seafaring pirates. Others will complain how lizardfolk raiding parties have always kept the town's prosperity in check. To these naysayers, I reply that an increased military presence is an obtainable goal. It just requires more money.

More money grants us larger docks to house naval warships. More money provides us the necessary muscle to form raiding parties of our own and finally eliminate the lizardfolk menace altogether! More money enables us to drain the newly-vacated lizardfolk marshes and turn them into bountiful farmlands. More money allows Daggerford to expand and grow into the thriving merchant center it was always destined to become!

Now, the naysayers will ask, "But where does this money come from?" It comes, my friends, from the only place it can: from you, the citizens of this fair town, who have a stake in making it a kinder, gentler place to live and raise a family. With a slight increase in taxes, we can recruit a larger military presence to supplement our already potent Griffons Mercenary Company. With Captain Dratharion as their master tactician, the Griffons shall soon rival the valiant Flaming Fists of Baldur's Gate!

The town has already begun bearing fruit from the Griffons' tireless labor. Bandits, though still active in the area, now know and fear the name "Dratharion" and shall soon begin to regard this stretch of the Trade Way as "poor pickings." Once that happens, and merchant caravans are able to pass freely in and out of Daggerford, we shall all benefit, financially and otherwise.

Have faith in me, fair citizens of Daggerford, and have faith in your town, for its outlook is golden!

The Brush of Barbs is so known because of its overgrown thickets of thorns that have overrun the trees and woods in the area, making trekking through the brush a very difficult endeavor. In some spots, the brush is impassable due to the volume of thorns. One such spot is the sequestered grove of the Stone Circle of Govan. Constructed by an elven druid named Govan Irfandel over 200 years ago, the stone circle of standing stones was meant to provide a meeting and ritual place for the local good-aligned druids. It was said that the trees, thickets, and vines were the ones who moved the heavy stones into place with accurate precision.
This wide leather belt once belonged to a knight called Sir Griswald who waged war against Lord Feldran to win the heart of Princess Soliana.
This simple wooden key was carved from a long hollow reed hardened among the coals of a hot fire. A few angular Draconic letters were carved into the wood while it was drying.

Lugard, a diminutive halfling wizard from Luskan was well known for his unusual sense of humor. As a practical joke, Lugard ventured to the nearby Ermite Quarry where he selected the five heaviest rocks. The clever little wizard enchanted these rocks with a powerful glamour which resisted all attempts to divine its true nature. He called these rocks Loadstones, and teleported them to various treasure hordes around the Realms where they might be discovered by wandering adventurers. The joke, of course, is that the Loadstones' glamour has no real magical powers; little Lugard chuckled merrily thinking about the unfortunate adventurers hauling his heavy Loadstones around the Sword Coast searching for a way to identify their magic. Unfortunately for Lugard, one of the Loadstones was found by Kurst, a savage barbarian with an astoundingly poor sense of humor. When Kurst learned that he had been tricked by a halfling wizard, he set out for Luskan carrying the Loadstone, and a heavy grudge. Three days later, poor Lugard was found dead at the bottom of Lake Luskan with a Loadstone tied around his ankles.
A thick coil of strong hemp rope is fastened securely around this heavy gray stone. The odd stone glows faintly, radiating a mysterious magical energy.
This heavy iron key opens one of the large cages in Nagnorm Stuffler's home.
A few scraps of yellowed vellum paper are wrapped around this old inkwell. Although the ink is of very poor quality, and clumps easily, the feathered quill is still serviceable.
This glass jar is filled with hundreds of small shiny fish. When emptied into a pool of water, these vicious fish will attack any creature unfortunate enough to be swimming in the water.
The drinker's skin coloring changes to match the surroundings, gaining a +10 competence bonus to any Hide checks.
Drinking this potion will cleanse your body of all harmful diseases.
Drinking this potion focuses your concentration in battle, giving a +20 bonus to your next attack.
Swallowing this fiery brew will cause the drinker to spew forth a huge gout of burning hot flame, very much like a dragon.
The drinker gains damage resistance 20/- against all elemental forms of damage. The effect ends after absorbing 30 points of damage from any single elemental type.
The drinker enters a rage similar to that of a barbarian. The drinker gains a +2 bonus to Strength and Constitution and a +1 bonus to Will saves, while suffering a -1 penalty to AC.

When consumed, this multicolored potion transforms the drinker into one of the following forms:

Giant spider
Troll
Umber hulk
Pixie
Zombie
This bottle of quicksilver was collected from a fountain in Edalseye's tower.

Lieutenant Skron kept a logbook detailing the Zhentarim's caravan raids along the Tradeway. The last few entries are as follows.

Faern & Young, from Scornubel - Silver and wine shipment.  Killed the guards and Young, enslaved Faern.

Boldug and Co. - Acquired shipment of furs and leathers. Convinced the cart driver it was in his best interest to join the Black Network trading branch.

Chessbalad Trading - A shipment of pots and jars not worth our time. Robbed cart driver instead.

Urgand Sisters Emporium - Ambushed one of our own caravans by mistake! We all had a good laugh. Captain Dratharion wasn't laughing though. Said I'd end up as Bugo's toilet scrubber if it happened again.

Calim's Exquisite Wares - Raiding party was set to take this shipment of gold, but the party mysteriously didn't return. Might be linked to that hero who helped those farmers.

This small golden amulet was given to you by Soliana, who called herself the Princess of Fanloc. She revealed to you that she was really a hawk transformed into a woman by a witch. This delicate necklace had the power to transform Soliana back into a hawk. However, after you helped her to find true love, she gave the necklace to you as a gift, saying that she has decided to remain by her love's side forever as a woman. Using the necklace will not transform you into a hawk, however, it will give you some of the hawk's abilities for a short period of time.
This key, marked with a large rune stone, belonged to a dark druid named Stegil.

Formed in a beachside forge from iron cooled by pure saltwater, this ring is covered with a thin rippling pattern, which is reminiscent of waves on the ocean. Touching the ring to your forehead, and speaking Umberlee's name will summon a water elemental to fight at your side.
This is the head of the One-Eyed Worg which plagued the Wild Pastures.
Although these velvet robes were once blessed by Bhaal's high priest, all that remain are tattered rags.

The long slender tines on this bone hairbrush are covered with strands of thick, greasy black hair. The brush's plain handle is decorated with several tattered feathers secured by a thin strip of well-chewed leather.

The wrinkled old lizardfolk shaman, Uzzak-Szalzik, carved this knife in the shape of a grinning dragon, its long sinuous body twisting around the knife's handle with the tip of its tail ending on the knife's long red metal blade. This knife is so precious to Uzzak-Szalzik that he used one of his own teeth to decorate its brown leather handle.
This crude map was sketched by a poor fisherwoman named Olree. The map shows how to successfully navigate the sea caves maze beneath Castle Exeltis.

Most Gnomes are not known for their keen sense of fashion, and Purfbin Doogrick is no exception. Despite its shocking colors and out-dated style, these eccentric robes offer Purfbin just what he needs: plenty of really deep pockets! Over the years, Purfbin has amassed a horde of seemingly-useless widgets which are stuffed into these pockets. Having just the right tool at hand has helped Purfbin out of some most uncomfortable situations in the past.

Over the years, Purfbin made several interesting customizations to his simple wooden crossbow. Although the weapon occasionally suffers strange mechanical glitches, such as a jammed locking clip, Purfbin is very proud of his creation. His latest enhancement was a clever rapid reload spring mechanism.

The warrior-mage, Janice Whentom, designed a shield that could be carried by an armored mage into battle. With its large size and protective magic, the shield allowed Janice to lend close support to her battalion's frontline fighters. However, the shield did not afford absolute protection, as is apparent by Janice's death from a stray arrow. In honor of her bravery, Janice's battalion donated the shield to her family, where it has resided until recently.

Jon Kellan, called "Gray Wolf" by his Wolf Pack mercenary subordinates, carried this shield from Icewind Dale to Waterdeep, where his troupe sought out employment. Renowned for their ferocity in battle, Jon and his Wolf Pack mercenaries were eventually hired on by one of the lords of Waterdeep. Their contract unfortunately got them entangled with a group of Zhentarim who far outnumbered the Gray Wolf and his soldiers. Even so, only three Zhentarim left the battlefield alive, which forced the Zhentarim to halt their latest plan for an assault on Waterdeep.

This colossal shield was unearthed from a tomb in the shifting sands of the Anauroch desert. The thief who uncovered the tomb attributed the shield's magical properties to his escape from the desert's punishing heat. Feeling emboldened by the shield's powers, the thief returned to the desert, this time with a small army of bloodthirsty brigands. He used this band to raid passing caravans for months until he was finally hunted down and killed, close to the same tomb from which he obtained the shield.

The heavy leather used to craft this suit of armor was cut from the living body of a tall white stag. As the deer died, crying with pain, its heartblood stained the leather dark red, the color of death. After the stained leather was set to dry, a dark druid named Stegil carved his personal coat of arms onto the chest piece: a bent and twisted blood tree. Finally, Malar, god of beasts, blessed this suit of armor with a unique set of combat powers.
This amulet was given to Veiti by her father Derval. It was once worn by the ancient defenders of Illefarn.

The great halfling matriarch, Twili Furfut the Elder, was well regarded, both for her cunning and for her seemingly limitless endurance on the battlefield. Although gray and well past her prime, Twili came to the aid of her town when barbarians attacked. However, when she struck out with her wooden staff, all present (including Twili Furfut herself) were surprised by the flurry of lightning bolts that rained down upon the attackers. Not known for her skill with magic, the townsfolk eventually decided that Twili's lightning must have originated from within the staff, which she had collected on some youthful escapade.

Nestled among the rugged Blade Cliffs along the Northern Sword Coast, lies an old stone castle badly in need of repair. Not long ago, the keepers of this castle, the Exeltis Clan, patiently cared for the rolling farm lands surrounding the old castle. When the good Lady Exeltis died, under somewhat suspicious circumstances,  castle Exeltis was passed along to the Lady's only child -- a young Lordling named Feldran.

Lord Exeltis, by all accounts a just and noble man, died from an infected wound when Feldran was a young boy. On his death-bed, Lord Exeltis gave his dagger, the famous Exeltis Blade, to young Feldran and made him promise to defend his mother.
