Years passed, and Lady Exeltis grew old while young Feldran grew into manhood. But without a father to guide him, the young Lordling grew wild, and soon forgot his promise to defend his mother.

On the darkest nights, when the moon hangs low in the trees, and the north wind howls over the cliffs, the bards of the Sword Coast whisper tales of how the young Lordling used this dagger, a gift from his dying father, to murder his mother.

This mighty lance was once wielded by Tolmarileth the Gray, a half-elven warrior with a deep-seeded hatred for all of dragonkind. This vendetta stemmed from the loss of his sister, Isha, at the hands of an adult wyrm called Vultimine the Black.

Unbeknownst to Isha, and the dragon's many other victims, Vultimine was actually an illusory creation of the wizard Kroundal. The summoned shadow's mere presence was enough to frighten its victims to death, causing their hair to turn white and their heart to stop. When Tolmarileth found and slew the wizard, he also destroyed the illusionist's draconic ally. However, Tolmarileth's history with dragons was only just getting started.

With lance in hand, Tolmarileth slew hundreds of dragons during his long life, and did not discriminate based on age or alignment. He eventually succumbed to an unlikely alliance between a bronze dragon and a blue dragon, who agreed to put aside their innate differences in order to fell this powerful dragonslayer.

Although some scholars believe that Tolmarileth's lance was laid within the tomb he shared with his sister, others believe that one of his slayers claimed the weapon as a prize. Due to the greedy nature of dragons, the second scenario seems the more likely of the two.

An elven huntress named Tasha Moonsong used this bow on many noteworthy hunting expeditions. During one such eventful trip, she apparently slew a roc from fifty yards with a barrage of well-placed arrows. Other stories tell of her hunting basilisks while wearing a blindfold to shield her eyes from their petrifying gaze. Tasha and her bow were last seen hunting prehistoric creatures in the Lizard Marsh near Daggerford.

This bone bow was created from the remains of a legendary porcupine. Arrows made from the creature's giant quills magically materialize when the bow is drawn. The druid Ginoldar Deathfang is credited with its creation and the slaying of the magical beast from which it was made.

During the gnoll siege of Reddansyr, arrows had become scarce. Had it not been for the unending barrage from Thousand Quills, the village certainly would have succumbed to the siege. Since that time, the bow's legendary status only continues to grow.

The sergeant-at-arms in the Zhentarim light infantry group called the "Ghost Ravens" carried this marvellous weapon into battle on numerous occasions. As the crossbow continued to draw the blood of Zhentil Keep's many enemies, its notoriety grew within the Zhentarim ranks. In fact, it is quite possible that this fame led to the wielder's untimely demise.

During a particularly bloody siege of Zhentil Keep, the sergeant-at-arms fell in battle, even though he was reportedly a good distance from the fighting. At around the same time, a new recruit mysteriously went missing, who many believe may have absconded with the mighty crossbow.

Created by a gnomish bowyer, this weapon was crafted from the heartwood of a treant and strung with hairs from the tail of a unicorn. The gnome was so impressed with his handiwork that he planned an elaborate exhibition for his fellow gnomes and anyone else in the area who wished to attend.

The performance consisted of the bowyer firing crossbow bolts at long range into water-filled barrels. Each time a bolt struck a barrel, the container literally exploded into bits, splashing the crowd of cheering onlookers. However, one particular onlooker, a half-orc bounty hunter, was not particularly amused or impressed.

This bounty hunter followed the bowyer back to his home and, with one strike from her hand axe, summarily ended the gnome's budding career as an entertainer. The bounty hunter also claimed the crossbow for her own, although she wisely avoided revealing its prowess to others.

This sling was used by an elven monk named Silence. The man's strange name was a result of his taking a vow of silence for so long that no one could remember his true name.

The sling earned its nickname during an altercation with an arcane archer who pursued the monk through a series of shadowy catacombs. After a lengthy chase, Silence feared the archer had him cornered. So he aimed the sling at the archer's slow-moving silhouette and fired with all the strength he could muster. The sling bullet careened off the stone wall and bounced its way down the hall, eventually striking the archer squarely in the chest.

Stunned from the direct assault to his shallow breastplate, the archer let his guard down for but a moment. Silence closed in and quickly subdued the archer with a blazing flurry of well-placed punches and roundhouse kicks.

Created from the horn of an ancient black dragon, the head of this hammer continually excretes a caustic acid. The Black Hammer, as it came to be known, was favored by a priestess of Bhaal named Niaal Sortan. In addition to its obvious uses in battle, the weapon served as a makeshift torture device for the priestess' many late-night rampages.

It was during one of these nocturnal excursions that Niaal was slain by a group of rangers waiting in ambush. However, due to the splash damage from the weapon's head, all received wounds so grave that no one survived the battle.

Hadrian Coltin was a procurer of rare items for Bintley's in Waterdeep. Hadrian's job often required that he "liberate" these items from their unwilling owners. This, of course, led to frequent scrapes with the owners' hired mercenaries, who guarded their masters' property with dogged determination. Eventually, Hadrian realized he needed to improve his swordplay skills if he were to remain alive.

He remembered that his father, a minor noble, had willed him a large bastard sword, called Bloody Longblade. The father's choice of weapon type was symbolic, as Hadrian's mother had been a serving wench in the local tavern. Despite the gift's hurtful intentions, Hadrian grew to value the weapon as an effective aid in prolonging his career as a collector.

This enchanted hammer was intended for use against a small army of skeletons that never materialized. Apparently, the dread necromancer who planned the summoning, took ill and had to call off the attack. However, the weapon's owner, a dwarf named Ascin Rockwall, found the hammer still had its uses.

When traveling through the Trollbark Forest, for example, Ascin became surrounded by a pack of hungry trolls. Without her magical hammer in hand, the trolls most certainly would have made a feast of Ascin that day. Instead, they found themselves pummelled into chunks that were summarily tossed onto Ascin's campfire like so much firewood.

The original owner of this weapon was slain while wielding it, after which their spirit became trapped within the blade courtesy of a rakshasa's malevolent curse. Shadow Cut has changed owners numerous times, often passing from one owner to the next via some form of misdeed or treachery.

The blade's most recent possessor was a vampire named Durismar, who favored elves as her targets. Each night, the vampire would track and hunt the elves in their forest home. Then, when her blood-thirst was slaked, she would retire to her underground lair to sleep away the daylight hours.

After years of terrorizing the inhabitants of the forest, Durismar the vampire was finally hunted down and slain by an elven war party. Her blade, Shadow Cut, was believed to have been locked away deep within the elven vaults.

Mungorat was wandering through the High Forest when he came upon a moonlit plateau ringed by bramble bushes. Tangled within the roots of these thorny hedges were the bones of various humanoid races. Apparently, the place had once served as a battleground for some large-scale conflict.

Mungorat liked the gloomy feel of the place and decided to make it his home. He built a hut out of the bones he collected and, using an axe he found stuck within the brambles, chopped up some tall trees for firewood.

Many years later, Mungorat's own skeletal remains were found within his bony hut by a group of wandering wood elves. Lying next to him was the great axe, which now bears 
his name.

This club was crafted for a hobgoblin chieftain named Slaul, who used it to keep his unruly minions in line. This effective deterrent, or "goblin herder" as Slaul liked to call it, eventually fell into the hands of the gnomes of Treeroot, who sorely needed a goblin herder of their own. For a time, the weapon was viewed as a symbol of leadership amongst the gnomes, until it was reclaimed by goblins during a bloody raid.

Doorknocker was the favored weapon of Pasi, a tiefling explorer. She often took the weapon into the Ruins of Tier Lathadun where she made use of its dual role as a circumventor of locked doors and slayer of the place's undead inhabitants.

Although Pasi earned her fortune in Tier Lathadun, she eventually slipped on a particularly rocky ledge and fell a thousand feet to her death. Doorknocker fell with her and was believed lost for all time within the depths of the earth.

This sword's name is thought to be the result of a bad translation of the weapon's cryptic runes. Today, most scholars feel that a correct translation would be something along the lines of "bad for some, but good for others." That translation seems more apt considering the blade's colorful history.

Milk and Honey's first owner was a brawny paladin named Kasis Col. The warrior carried the blade into numerous conflicts, although legend claims she never actually used it as intended. Apparently, the mere sight of the paladin wielding this powerful weapon caused opponents to back down without a fight.

The second owner of the blade, Sir Jolin Bassal, was not so lucky. For him, the longsword seemed a veritable magnet for violent offenders, resulting in Bassal having to slay some two hundred foes in mortal combat. Eventually, Bassal met his end fighting a yuan-ti abomination aboard a sinking ship some miles off the Sword Coast. It is believed the sword accompanied its owner to the bottom of the sea where it now resides.

Members of the Wheloon militia would often relate the story of how this item came into their possession. 
During a raid on a smuggler's den just outside the city, the militia came upon a middle-aged gentleman 
sitting high atop a pile of stolen goods. Not taking notice of the soldiers, the man focused on a small 
stick he used to tap out a rhythmic beat on the chests and barrels around him. When told to surrender, the 
man refused, causing the militia guards to joke how the fellow seemed ready to fight off an entire army 
with nothing but a "twig" in his hand. Had they known what would happen next, the soldiers might have 
retracted their joke, as the entire unit was engulfed within a blazing inferno.

This rod was brought to Faerûn by an elder earth elemental, who left it in the care of a gnomish apprentice conjurer, named Elbix, explaining to him its limited power. At his settlement's local tavern, Elbix would often exaggerate to awe-struck ears the wondrous powers of his rod. It brought him a measure of respect and often several rounds of free drinks.

Several years later, he finally had occasion to use it. A great ettin chief, by the name of Gnarltooth, was fast approaching the gnomish lands, leading a gang of ettins. This prompted the gnome leader to hurriedly summon Elbix and his mighty rod to save the gnomish settlement. By this time, the conjurer's tall tales of the weapon had swollen it to legendary proportion. What made matters worse was that none of the other gnomes were bothering to prepare any defenses at all and instead pinned their expectations on the Stonestick to obliterate the monsters within minutes.

A nervous Elbix saw no hope of survival when he was left to face the oncoming creatures. Gnarltooth easily snatched up the thrashing gnome for a closer look but accidentally received the Stonestick in the eye. This caused the monster to trip backwards and, incredibly, impale itself on its own spear. With the defeat of their leader, the other ettins fled. The result was that Elbix became the luckiest gnome in the world and, intending to keep it that way, tossed the Stonestick into the river at the earliest opportunity.

This axe was created for the mighty dwarven chief known as King Taik. The weapon's sole purpose was to keep at bay the orcish hordes that continuously threatened Taik's subterranean realm. It was forged with the blood of the orcish sorcerer Sajifot, and inherited some of that spellcaster's bloodthirsty nature.

Blood Frenzy is best known for cutting off the head of Kumon, the leader of an orcish horde, thus breaking the horde's morale and causing their eventual extinction. The axe was buried with King Taik in a secret tomb and is believed lost for all time.

Knives of this sort, with their long, thin metal blades, are often employed by dedicated taxidermists to assist in their delicate craft. Typically, these knives are very personal possessions, and as such are stamped with their owner's initials. This particular blade is stamped with the initials: "N.S."

It is believed the hero Scaldulin pulled this blade from the heart of a glacier and later used its powers to slay a legion of demons in the Battle of the Thousand Dead. The blade was also responsible for severing the hand of the lich, Scaroth the Warped, during the razing of Blackmoor. However, the blade is best known for being plunged into the heart of the solar, Arazium, during Scaldulin's fall from grace and eventual transformation into a death knight.

Verdicil, a well-known assassin in Waterdeep, received this poison-tipped dagger as a gift from the guild master upon completing her two-hundredth contract. Shortly thereafter, Verdicil disappeared from Waterdeep without a trace, causing many to suspect foul play.

However, Verdicil later resurfaced as an emissary for Nemsé. Outraged by his former pupil's abandonment of the guild, the guild master sent nine assassins to murder Verdicil in her sleep. The next morning, the guild master received a delivery of nine crates, each containing a severed head. They were the heads of his nine assassins.

Fashioned for the elven mistress Lissial, after the infamous sword, Veiled Tears, this lesser cousin was created by an apprentice of the elven smith Quilin. Though originally called Gentle Rain, the sword earned the name Longbite when it helped Lissial fight her way out of a hill giant ambush. Seeing that she was outmatched, she lunged at the leader and swung at his neck, cleaving the giant's head from his shoulders in one fell stroke. The remaining giants fled in a panic.

Created in Daggerford, this mace was specifically designed to quell the constant attacks by the lizardfolk from the nearby Lizard Marsh. The mace's owner, Roline "The Hand" Tark, was a caravan guard who used the weapon to great success. While handily guarding the wares of her clients from lizardfolk raiding parties, she began to collect the teeth of her reptilian victims. These she sold to collectors for a tidy sum, helping her amass a small fortune. Oddly enough, it was the lizardfolk who gave the mace its name, out of respect for both the weapon and its owner.

This flail belonged to a priestess named Felina Tatch, whose one goal in life was to release undead souls from the torment that binds them to the Material Plane. Felina's extreme devotion to this task eventually caused her to run afoul of the vampire Milikaia who slew the priestess and subjugated her will.

Not long afterwards, Felina was seen wandering the graveyard near her hometown where, oddly enough, she resumed her quest to hunt down and destroy the living dead. The fate of the vampire Milikaia is unknown.

Forged from the metal of a meteorite by an evil, nameless derro, the sword called Starfire has had a long string of unlucky owners. After serving the derro, the sword was claimed in a raid by a group of marauding mountain dwarves. Later, the sword's glowing flames betrayed the dwarves' location to a troglodyte war party, which claimed the weapon as spoils in a hard-fought victory.
